Websites, ideas, particular photos, your dog, experiments, questions, anything! It's all welcome here. Also side note: sorry for not keeping this up to date. Got pretty busy there for a bit.

From Thanksgiving to New Years every year I take a break from (most) social media. Facebook, Instagram, Tumblr, and Twitter. My wife changes all of my passwords (she missed this one!). It's great and the world doesn't even end!

I go through my stack of photobooks, organize my Lightroom catalogs, and get ready for the new year. I usually finish up a project or start one. This year I finished up my project (I posted about it here already https://voat.co/v/photography/comments/678173 ) so I'm just working on kind of resetting and figuring out next year.

Some photobooks I'm excited for: http://imgur.com/a/BZEAg
* Alec Soth's (almost) complete collection in minibook form. I wasn't lucky enough to get Sleeping By The Mississippi the first time around so this will have to do. Signed copy with a bunch of prints.
* Aperture workshop series books are awesome.
* I was recommended this book Tuned In which has some spectacular photos of yesteryear similar to how people are buried in their phones today, this is in the 70's where people were buried in their TV's. Cool to see the parallels and the book was 4$

One thing I do in December is also hold a party at a brewery with a bunch of different photographers. You must bring prints. Must. No digital. We pass around the stacks of prints and people initial the backs of ones they like. It really is a fun editing process! Someone told me Josef Koudelka uses this method and I know a lot of Magnum guys do. I did it with a bunch of Magnum guys in October for my project and it was fun. You can listen to a recording I took at a little get together with Peter Van Agtmael talk about it here. (David Alan Harvey, Michael Christopher Brown and a few others in the background https://soundcloud.com/robtimko/peter-van-agtmael-at-david-alan-harveys)

I bought some microphone equipment...no idea what I'm going to do with it.

I bought some printing equipment to make my own prints and I'm very very VERY surprised at the quality. I mean, wow. For a cheapo printer with some good paper (and I'm a REAL pretentious print guy!) they are awesome.
